newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, long-term swaps active.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, long-term swaps active.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah was steady against the dollar in slow late trading on Thursday, with the focus on long-term swaps, dealers said.

One European bank dealer said the market was dull after the central bank raised its fixing by one point. But he said the long-end swap market was well offered. "It's a slow day apart from people trying to drive the market by creating false rumours," he said, adding that the rumours had little effect.
Dealers said Singapore players were spreading false rumours that there was a riot in Jakarta. No violence was reported in the city.
One Singapore dealer said players were more cautious this time and did not react to the rumours after being misled by unfounded reports last week about President Suharto's health.
He said swap rates responded with some small increases while the spot rate generally shrugged off the rumours.

Spot rupiah declined briefly to 2,407.00/07.75 from an opening of 2,405.50/06.25, but settled later at 2,406.6/06.8 at 0850 GMT. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,405.8/06.2 and 2,405.2/05.6, respectively.
"I have basically no view where the rupiah is going. The market appears to be pretty mixed, no clear trend," he said.
